identity.title: Non-Convex Federated Optimization under Cost-Aware Client Selection

problem.claim: Compare and design non-convex federated optimization methods while accounting for communication and local computation costs under different client-selection strategies.

gap.claim: Existing optimization metrics typically do not distinguish client-selection strategies with different practical communication costs.

contributions.claim: Introduces a federated optimization model that quantifies communication and local computation complexities and assigns distinct costs to several client-selection strategies.
Proposes an algorithm based on inexact composite gradients, a carefully constructed estimator, and a special auxiliary-subproblem procedure.
Introduces Recursive-Gradient as a general technique for potentially improving error bounds of conditionally unbiased estimators, and applies it to create RG-SAGA.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors state that the proposed algorithm attains the best-known communication and local complexities among existing non-convex federated optimization methods within their cost model.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report a new variance bound for SAGA that shows it can exploit functional similarity.
The authors report that applying Recursive-Gradient to SAGA yields RG-SAGA with an improved error bound relative to the original SAGA estimator.
The authors report best-known communication and local complexities for their algorithm among existing non-convex federated optimization methods in the introduced setting.

narrative_sequence.summary: Federated optimization algorithms use random-subset, all-client, or hybrid client selection strategies.
Existing comparison metrics generally overlook the differing communication costs induced by these strategies.
The paper introduces a model that quantifies communication and local computation and links each supported strategy to a distinct cost.
Within this model, it proposes a non-convex optimization algorithm using inexact composite gradients, a gradient estimator, and an auxiliary-subproblem procedure.
Starting from a new SAGA variance bound, the paper proposes Recursive-Gradient and derives RG-SAGA with an improved error bound.

source_observation.claim: The abstract first identifies a mismatch between standard comparisons and strategy-dependent communication costs, then introduces an explicit cost model before presenting the algorithm.

lessons.interpretation: A problem framing can make an algorithmic contribution more specific by defining the operational cost being optimized before claiming comparative performance.
lessons.application: Define client-selection regimes and their communication/local-computation costs before reporting complexity comparisons for a federated method.
lessons.exception: This framing is unsuitable when the target deployment has uniform costs or when the study concerns statistical quality without computational resource constraints.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the exact complexity bounds, assumptions, or baseline methods underlying the best-known comparison.
It does not provide quantitative values or conditions for the SAGA and RG-SAGA variance/error-bound improvements.
The meaning and operational scope of functional similarity are not defined in the abstract.
